name: SaaS & Subscription
tagline: MRR, ARR, churn, expansion and net revenue retention from monthly account snapshots
description: Monthly MRR snapshots and movement reports from Stripe, Chargebee, Recurly, Razorpay Subscriptions, ChartMogul, Baremetrics or a billing data warehouse, and subscription lists with plan, seats and status.

fields.label: Snapshot month
fields.description: The month (or snapshot date) each row describes; MRR is read at the latest snapshot in a period.

fields.label: Opening MRR
fields.description: MRR at the start of the month (the previous month's closing MRR).

fields.label: MRR
fields.description: Closing monthly recurring revenue of the account in that month; annual plans divided by 12.

fields.label: Contraction MRR
fields.description: MRR lost to downgrades, as a positive amount.

fields.label: Churned MRR
fields.description: MRR lost to cancellations, as a positive amount.

subDomains.name: Monthly MRR snapshots
subDomains.description: One row per account per month with opening and closing MRR and the movements between them.

subDomains.name: Subscription list
subDomains.description: One row per account or subscription with plan, seats, MRR and churn status.

kpis.name: MRR
kpis.definition: Monthly recurring revenue at the latest snapshot in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of MRR on the latest month in view (semi-additive)

variants.label: ARR ÷ 12, latest month
variants.caveat: No MRR column, so MRR is ARR ÷ 12.

variants.label: Current snapshot, churned excluded
variants.caveat: No snapshot month, so the file is read as one current snapshot and churned accounts are left out.

variants.label: Single snapshot
variants.caveat: No snapshot month, so the file is read as one point-in-time snapshot.

pitfalls: MRR is semi-additive: each period shows its latest month, never a sum of months.
In breakdowns each plan or account shows MRR at its own latest month, so keep churned accounts in the file with zero MRR in the month they leave; otherwise they keep their last MRR.

kpis.name: ARR
kpis.definition: Annual recurring revenue: the latest MRR run-rate times twelve.

kpis.name: Net new MRR
kpis.definition: Change in MRR from all movements: new, expansion and reactivation minus contraction and churn.
kpis.formula: New + expansion + reactivation − contraction − churned MRR

variants.label: New + expansion − contraction − churned
variants.caveat: No reactivation column, so returning accounts are not counted separately.

variants.label: Closing − opening MRR
variants.caveat: No movement columns, so net new MRR is closing minus opening MRR summed over account-months.

kpis.name: Net revenue retention
kpis.definition: Share of opening MRR still billed at month end by the same accounts, counting upgrades and downgrades but not new business (a monthly rate; over several months, the opening-weighted average month).
kpis.formula: (Opening + expansion − contraction − churned MRR) ÷ opening MRR

benchmark.note: Indicative: annual NRR above 100% (expansion outweighing churn) is the usual bar for strong B2B SaaS. This figure is monthly, so 100% is its break-even point.

pitfalls: Monthly NRR is not the 12-month cohort NRR investors quote; compounding twelve months of 99% gives about 89%.

kpis.name: Gross MRR churn
kpis.definition: Share of opening MRR lost to cancellations and downgrades in the month, before any expansion (a monthly rate).

variants.label: Churned ÷ opening
variants.caveat: No contraction column, so only cancellations count.

kpis.name: Logo churn
kpis.definition: Share of paying accounts that cancelled: the monthly logo churn rate for a single month, and over longer periods the share of accounts active at the start of any month that churned within it.
kpis.formula: Churned accounts ÷ accounts with opening MRR above zero

variants.label: Churned accounts ÷ accounts with opening MRR
Churned accounts ÷ all accounts
variants.caveat: No opening MRR, so the base is every account in view: a cumulative churn share, not a monthly rate.

benchmark.note: Indicative monthly range: enterprise-focused SaaS tends toward the bottom and SMB products toward the top.

kpis.name: Active accounts
kpis.definition: Accounts paying at the latest snapshot in the period.
kpis.formula: Distinct accounts with MRR above zero on the latest month in view

variants.label: Paying accounts not flagged churned
variants.caveat: No snapshot month: counts accounts with MRR above zero that are not flagged as churned.

variants.label: Accounts with MRR above zero
variants.caveat: No snapshot month: counts every account with MRR above zero.

pitfalls: Active accounts are a snapshot: they come from the latest month in each period, never a count across months.

kpis.name: Average revenue per account
kpis.definition: MRR per paying account at the latest snapshot.
pitfalls: ARPA rises when small accounts churn even if no one pays more; read it next to logo churn.

kpis.name: New MRR
kpis.definition: MRR from accounts that started paying in the period.

kpis.name: Expansion MRR
kpis.definition: Extra MRR from existing accounts through upgrades, add-ons and more seats.

kpis.name: Contraction MRR
kpis.definition: MRR lost from accounts that downgraded but stayed.

kpis.name: Churned MRR
kpis.definition: MRR lost from accounts that cancelled.

kpis.name: SaaS quick ratio
kpis.definition: MRR gained for every unit of MRR lost.

variants.label: (New + expansion) ÷ (contraction + churned)
variants.caveat: No reactivation column, so returning accounts are not counted separately.

benchmark.note: Indicative: above 1 means MRR is growing; a ratio around 4 is the widely quoted mark of efficient early-stage growth.

kpis.name: New accounts
kpis.definition: Accounts that started paying in the period.
kpis.formula: Distinct accounts with new MRR above zero

variants.label: Accounts in their first month in the file
variants.caveat: No new-MRR column: accounts count in the month they first appear, so accounts already present when the file starts look new.

kpis.name: Churned accounts
kpis.definition: Accounts that cancelled in the period.
kpis.formula: Distinct accounts with churned MRR above zero

variants.label: Accounts flagged as churned
variants.caveat: Uses the churned flag; if the flag repeats on every row of a churned account, earlier months count it too.

variants.label: Accounts with a churn date
variants.caveat: Counts accounts that have a churn date.

kpis.name: Seats
kpis.definition: Paid seats or licences at the latest snapshot in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of seats on paying accounts in the latest month (semi-additive)

variants.label: Seats on paying accounts, latest month
Seats, latest month
variants.caveat: No MRR column, so seats on non-paying accounts in the latest month count too.

variants.label: Seats on accounts not flagged churned
variants.caveat: No snapshot month: the file is read as one current snapshot.

variants.label: Seats, single snapshot
variants.caveat: No snapshot month, so the file is read as one point-in-time snapshot.

kpis.name: Gross revenue retention
kpis.definition: Share of opening MRR kept after cancellations and downgrades, ignoring expansion (a monthly rate).

kpis.name: Reactivation MRR
kpis.definition: MRR from previously churned accounts that came back.

kpis.name: Opening MRR
kpis.definition: MRR at the start of each month, summed over the months in view: the base for churn and retention rates.

kpis.name: MRR per seat
kpis.definition: Average monthly price paid per seat at the latest snapshot.

charts.title: MRR over time
charts.reason: Closing MRR per month: each point is the latest snapshot in the period, never a sum across months, drawn as a continuous line with a soft fill.

charts.title: MRR movements
charts.reason: Four flows per month on one currency axis: grouped columns compare what was gained with what was lost, month by month.

charts.title: MRR by signup year
charts.reason: MRR adds up across accounts, so stacking each month's closing MRR by signup year (a layer cake) shows how much of today's revenue comes from older versus newer customers.

charts.title: Net revenue retention
charts.reason: A monthly rate recomputed from each month's opening MRR and movements, drawn as a line; it is never averaged across accounts.

charts.title: Gross MRR churn vs logo churn
charts.reason: Two monthly rates on the same percentage axis: lines show whether the revenue lost and the share of customers lost move together.

charts.title: MRR by plan
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a handful of plans: a donut shows each plan's share of current MRR.

charts.title: MRR by region
charts.reason: Current MRR compared across regions: sorted horizontal bars, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: ARPA by plan
charts.reason: A per-account average compared across plans: bars of ARPA recomputed per plan from MRR and active accounts; plans with under 20 rows are hidden.

charts.title: Logo churn by plan
charts.reason: A rate compared across plans: logo churn recomputed per plan; plans with under 30 rows are hidden as too small to judge.

charts.title: Seats vs MRR by account
charts.reason: Two measures per account at the latest snapshot: a scatter with a trendline exposes accounts paying far more or less per seat than the rest.

charts.title: MRR concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How dependent recurring revenue is on a few accounts: each account's share of current MRR as columns and the cumulative share as a line on one 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Top accounts
charts.reason: Several measures per account: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: MRR, ARR, active accounts and seats are semi-additive: each period shows the latest month's snapshot, never a sum across months.
Annual and multi-year contracts must be normalised to a monthly amount (contract value ÷ months) before they enter MRR; booking a full annual invoice in one month inflates MRR and fakes churn later.
Contraction and churned MRR are expected as positive amounts (money lost); exports that store them as negatives flip the sign of net new MRR and the churn rates.
Churn and retention here are monthly rates; over a quarter or a year they are averages of months, not cohort retention. A steady 2% monthly logo churn compounds to roughly 21% a year.
Survivorship: older cohorts contain only the accounts that stayed, so their MRR per account looks better than that of newer cohorts.
A plan or region with a few dozen accounts swings by whole percentage points when one account churns; rate charts hide groups that are too small.
